solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Troublemaker took initiative and made impression

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little troublemaker
to act is to take the initiative and do something, past tense here

explanation.surface: Someone who stirred things up by taking charge left their mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made impression' is read as a verb phrase: something impacted has been pressed firmly in.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacted means pressed or wedged firmly in, as when a mark has been driven into a surface.

clue.text: Traveller to ruin company car (VW)

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
the Polo is a small car made by Volkswagen

explanation.surface: A journey is spoilt when the firm's Volkswagen breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed (VW) tells you which make of car to think of: Volkswagen's Polo hatchback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant who journeyed to China in the thirteenth century is the archetypal explorer and wanderer.

clue.text: Article penned by friend making one calm

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed as if in a pen, so the article sits inside the word for friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing by a companion soothes its reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making one' is a link; the definition is the verb 'calm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay fears is to quieten or soothe them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Matrix treated with dye in preservation process

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemical mixture and colouring are used to keep a specimen intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges the nine letters of MATRIX and DYE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of stuffing and mounting dead animal skins so they keep a lifelike look.

clue.text: Wicked protest — prison shortly follows

indicators.note: follows places the shortened prison word after the protest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or demonstration

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter of the slang word comes off

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison

explanation.surface: A nasty march ends with demonstrators soon behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison; 'shortly' clips its last letter, and 'follows' sets the result after the protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devilish or fiendish is wicked in the extreme.

clue.text: Superficial damage created by monster in school

indicators.note: in places the monster inside the short form of school

parts.note: an orc is a fantasy monster

explanation.surface: A beast loose in a classroom causes only surface harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorch is a burn mark that affects only the surface of something.

clue.text: Run into worthless people, disorderly group

indicators.note: into puts the run abbreviation inside the word for worthless people

parts.note: scum is a contemptuous word for worthless people
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: You bump into lowlifes in an unruly crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crush of people jostling together.

clue.text: One being kept in suspense a year, not doing any work at all?

definitions.text: not doing any work at all?

indicators.note: being kept in means the numeral sits inside the phrase for suspense

parts.note: on hold means held in suspense, waiting
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone left waiting for a whole year is effectively idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being kept in' puts I inside ON HOLD to give ONHOLID, then A and Y follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away on vacation means taking a break from your job entirely.

clue.text: Detectives collecting a new dog maybe

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the detectives' letters surround the others

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police investigators pick up a stray hound.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: A canid is any member of the dog family, so a dog is one example, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Long-winded publicist — drivel ultimately getting one cross

parts.note: a PR person is a pro, short for public relations officer

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of the word drivel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A rambling PR man talks nonsense until someone gets annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix speech or writing uses far too many words and is tediously verbose.

clue.text: Trader to sing at the end of season with total amount disposed of

indicators.note: at the end of places the singing word after what remains of the season
disposed of means got rid of, so the total is removed from the season

parts.note: summer is a season
a sum is a total amount
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper sings at summer's close once all the money is spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' removes the total from the season; 'at the end of' tacks the singing word on behind; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a dealer who buys and sells goods.

clue.text: Element in mob — men duly bundled off

indicators.note: bundled off means hustled away roughly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Police duly bundle away a crowd of thugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bundled off' rearranges MOB, MEN and DULY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Molybdenum is a metallic chemical element, number 42, used in hard steels.

clue.text: Youngster with yen for older female

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, the yen

explanation.surface: A young man fancies an older woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like longing, matching the surface romance, but it is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite word for a grown woman.

clue.text: Magician's fiddle

explanation.surface: A conjurer plays the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magician's' reads as a possessive but is 'Magician is': a witch doctor or medicine man. Fiddle means falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor can be a sorcerer or healer working magic, as in witch doctor; to doctor accounts is to falsify or tamper with them.

clue.text: Assume a role offering censure

explanation.surface: Playing a character draws criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses split the phrase differently: take a part means act a role; take apart means criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a part means playing a character in a play; taking someone apart means criticising them severely.

clue.text: Baddie keeping quiet by river where money is handed over

indicators.note: keeping means holding in, so the call for quiet goes inside the baddie

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
SH is the call for quiet
the Esk is a river name in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A villain lies low beside a river at the spot where cash changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the river on; the Esk is a common British river name.
explanation.definitionFit: A till counter in a shop or bank is the place customers pay.

clue.text: Practised manoeuvres for all 32 on board?

explanation.surface: Rehearsed moves suit every chessman on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: A chess set has 32 men; the question mark flags reading the answer as 'set (of) pieces'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsed plays from corners and free kicks in football are standard routines; a complete chess set holds thirty-two men.

clue.text: Shyness — it makes this getting together tricky

indicators.note: tricky means awkward or deceptive, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being bashful makes meeting people difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges SHYNESS and IT; 'makes this' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthesis is a combining of parts into a whole, a coming together.

clue.text: Absurd boss of the Poplar 'erald not named?

indicators.note: not here means without, so the abbreviation for named is dropped

parts.note: Poplar is a district in London's East End, home of the cockney
N is an abbreviation for named
ED is an editor, the boss of a newspaper such as a Herald

explanation.surface: Is the East End local paper's editor anonymous and ridiculous?
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'erald mimics cockney speech; a cockney Ed would edit it. Poplar is in London's East End. 'not' drops N from COCKNEYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockeyed means crooked and, by extension, nonsensical or crazy.

clue.text: Mess American dumped outside old city by a Great Lake

indicators.note: outside means the remaining letters wrap around the old abbreviation
dumped means thrown out, so the American abbreviation is removed

parts.note: detritus is debris or mess

explanation.surface: An American rubbish heap surrounds an ancient lakeside settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumped' takes US from DETRITUS, leaving DETRIT; 'outside' wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michigan city stands on the Detroit River between Lakes St Clair and Erie, one of the Great Lakes.

clue.text: Making an effort can be irksome

explanation.surface: Attempting something can be tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means attempting; a trying person or situation is annoying and wearing.

clue.text: Commander horrified to lose good man?

indicators.note: to lose means without, so the saint's abbreviation drops out

parts.note: aghast means horrified
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Is the leader appalled at losing a virtuous man?
explanation.definitionFit: An agha is a title for a military officer or chief in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Explanation of surprise with these destroying the birds

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise; the clue as held reads explanation

indicators.note: destroying means wiping out, so the second word is removed from the first

explanation.surface: Wow, these wrecked the birds!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explanation' is presumably 'Exclamation' as the setter meant: GEE! 'destroying' removes THE from THESE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large web-footed waterfowl.

clue.text: Party chair slammed for system precluding leading women

indicators.note: slammed means battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The party's chairman is attacked for a male-dominated structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriarchy is a social order where men hold power and women are shut out from leadership.

clue.text: One may be sustaining market, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for market is said aloud and sounds like the answer

parts.note: to peddle is to market or hawk goods

explanation.surface: Someone may be keeping a market going, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: A piano's sustaining lever, worked by the foot, holds notes on.
explanation.definitionFit: On a piano, the right-hand foot lever is the sustain device holding notes on.

clue.text: A bishop repeatedly involved in religious instruction as teacher

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside the religious instruction abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject

indicators.note: repeatedly means the bishop's letter appears twice

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop often takes part in religious lessons as a tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is religious instruction, the old British school subject; 'repeatedly' doubles B; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher of the law.

clue.text: Two in opposition giving an ambiguous answer

explanation.surface: Two opposing parties give a noncommittal reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literally two opposite words; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words are direct opposites; replying with both is a hedged, equivocal response.

clue.text: Artist as trainee is needing tutor initially

parts.note: a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word tutor

explanation.surface: A painter in training needs a teacher to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso and Braque were painters of the Cubist movement.

clue.text: It's consonant with hidden talent

indicators.note: with here means containing, so the letters are carried inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A gift you keep secret fits in nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consonant with' looks like 'in keeping with'; in fact the definition is a sound such as D or T made with the teeth. 'It's' and 'with' join.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental is a consonant articulated with the tongue against the teeth, such as T or D.

clue.text: Wine in sampling found to be most toothsome

indicators.note: in places the wine inside the word for sampling

parts.note: a test is a sampling or trial
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A wine at a tasting proves the most delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means delicious, so the most toothsome is the most flavoursome.
